newsitem.title: GERMANY: German budget, tax talks make no progress.
newsitem.headline: German budget, tax talks make no progress.

text.p: Germany's ruling coalition made little headway on Tuesday in talks on tax reform and the 1997 budget that have badly strained Chancellor Helmut Kohl's 14-year centre-right government, officials said.

Kohl has planned another session on Tuesday evening with leaders of his Christian Democrats (CDU), the Bavarian Christian Social Union (CSU) and the liberal free Democrats (FDP) to continue the search for a compromise, they said.

Finance Minister and CSU chairman Theo Waigel has been pitted for weeks in a struggle with the pro-business FDP over how to find several billion marks to finance the 1997 budget without overstepping the Maastricht limits on public borrowing.
The chancellor demonstratively threw his weight behind Waigel on Monday when he returned to work from an eight-day Far East tour.

But FDP leaders, especially former economics minister Juergen Moellemann, continued to insist that some FDP deputies would vote down the government's budget if it did not agree to cut back a hated "solidarity tax" for eastern Germany in 1998.
Waigel and Kohl do not want to pledge this so far in advance.
